title: जनै पूर्णिमाको सांस्कृतिक उपादेयता
nepali: संस्कृत शब्दको परिस्कृत एवम् परिमार्जित संस्कारहरूको समभावका रुपमा संस्कृति शब्द व्यवहृत, प्रयोग र प्रचलनमा रहेको छ । संस्कारले शुद्धिक्रिया जसमा मानिसका चारित्रिक अवगुण, दोष कमी कमजोरीहरूलाई हटाई परिष्कार गर्ने काम एवम् मानिस जैविक प्राणी भएकाले यसलाई सामाजिक प्राणी बनाउनमा योगदान दिने तत्त्वहरूको अर्थ संवहन गरेको हुन्छ । समाजको मानसक्रिया सम्बद्ध सम्पूर्ण तत्त्वहरूको समग्र रूप नै संस्कृतिका रुपमा परिभाषित रहेका छ । जनै पूर्णिमालाई हिन्दू तागाधारीहरूले अनिवार्य पालना गर्नुपर्ने संस्कारको रूपमा लिइए पनि प्राचीन वैदिक साहित्यमा संस्कार प्रचलनमा नरही लौकिक युगमा तर उपनयन कर्मसँग सम्बन्धित भएर आएको पाइन्छ । नेपालमा तागाधारीहरूले मनाउने जनैपूर्णिमाका सम्बन्धमा विभिन्न कथनहरू रहेका छन् । जनै पूर्णिमाका दिन शरीरमा धारण गरिएको जनै फेर्नुका अतिरिक्त रक्षाबन्धनका रुपमा  हातमा रातो पहेंलो डोरोसमेत बाँध्ने प्रचलन रहेको छ । यिनै संस्कारहरू मध्ये मानव जन्मका अशुद्धिहरू हटाउन एउटा निश्चित उमेर पुगेपछि गुरु थापेर ब्रतबन्ध (उपनयन) संस्कार गरी यज्ञोपवित (जनै) धारण गरेर सामाजिक र धार्मिक सबै प्रकारका कार्यहरू गर्न योग्य हुने कार्यलाई हिन्दू तागाधारी समुदायले पालना गरेर आइरहेका छन् । यसरी निश्चित विधिविधान सहित विशेष समारोहको आयोजना गरी पहिलोपल्ट धारण गरिएको जनैलाई वर्षै पिच्छे परिवर्तन गर्नुपर्ने दिनको रूपमा ‘‘जनैपूर्णिमा’’ रहेको छ । यसदिन शारीरिक रूपमा शुद्ध भई पवित्र जलाशय वा नदीमा स्नान गरी ब्राह्मण गुरुद्वारा प्रदान गरिएको जनै धारण गर्नुपर्ने प्रचलन रहेको छ ।
american_english: The word 'culture' is in use, practice and circulation as an equivalent of the refined and modified rites of the Sanskrit word. Rite conveys the meaning of purification, in which the work of removing and refining a person's character flaws, faults, shortcomings and weaknesses is done, as well as the elements that, because humans are biological beings, contribute to making them social beings. The totality of all elements connected with the mental activity of society is defined as culture. Although Janai Purnima is taken by Hindu sacred-thread wearers as a rite that must be compulsorily observed, it is found that the rite was not in practice in ancient Vedic literature, but came into being in the worldly age in connection with the upanayana (initiation) rite. There are various accounts regarding Janai Purnima observed by sacred-thread wearers in Nepal. On the day of Janai Purnima, apart from changing the sacred thread worn on the body, there is a practice of tying a red and yellow thread on the hand as raksha bandhan. Among these rites, the Hindu sacred-thread-wearing community has been observing the act of becoming eligible to perform all kinds of social and religious works by, after reaching a certain age to remove the impurities of human birth, having a guru perform the bratabandha (upanayana) rite and wearing the yajnopavita (sacred thread). Thus, Janai Purnima is the day on which the sacred thread first worn with a special ceremony following definite procedures must be changed every year. On this day there is a practice of becoming physically pure, bathing in a sacred reservoir or river, and wearing the sacred thread given by a Brahmin guru.

informal_english: The word 'culture' basically gets used as a stand-in for the refined and modified rites of the Sanskrit word. A rite is about purification — cleaning out a person's bad traits, faults and weaknesses — and the stuff that turns us from biological creatures into social ones. Culture, in short, is the whole of everything tied to a society's mental life. Hindu sacred-thread wearers treat Janai Purnima as a rite you have to observe, but it turns out it wasn't around in ancient Vedic literature; it showed up later, in the worldly age, tied to the upanayana initiation. There are all sorts of stories about Janai Purnima as observed by thread-wearers in Nepal. On the day itself, besides changing the sacred thread you wear, people tie a red and yellow thread on the hand as raksha bandhan. Among these rites, the thread-wearing community has kept up the practice of becoming eligible for all social and religious duties by, once you reach a certain age to clear the impurities of birth, having a guru do the bratabandha (upanayana) rite and wearing the yajnopavita (sacred thread). So Janai Purnima is the day the sacred thread first worn in a special ceremony following set procedures has to be changed every year. On that day people purify themselves physically, bathe in a sacred pond or river, and wear the sacred thread given by a Brahmin guru.
